originality.rationale: The source establishes the logistic fold and the lifted graph but restricts its bounded-orbit theorem to b<4. The current theorem treats the natural excluded b=4 endpoint and derives an explicit stationary tail, a sharp moment transition, and in particular the exact entire law and nonconvergent dyadic centered family of the critical-half-interval recovery time conditioned on a very large vertical observation. The latter is not the same as classical stationary return-time or extreme-value limit laws. Another rational planar source has a different affine first component. Targeted published-result and primary-literature comparisons found no statement that implies the combined endpoint/conditional law. The basic logistic conjugacy and arcsine density are explicitly credited to known theory; priority beyond indexed and inspected material remains open.

value.rationale: The published folding theorem stops at b<4, whereas at the natural critical endpoint the first coordinate remains in a bounded logistic interval but the vertical observable becomes noncompact. The exact invariant tail/moment transition and the complete logarithmic post-burst recovery law distinguish stationary distribution from deterministic temporal response. The return threshold t=1/2 is the model's unique logistic critical point, not an arbitrary slice; its sharp finite-threshold and dyadic phase law is a natural rare-event invariant, potentially useful for comparing singular-observable extremes and intermittent recovery. The full exact conditional law provides information beyond the known invariant graph and classical one-time logistic density.
